partnerCats.title: Partner categories
partnerCats.help: What kind of trade a partner is. On the customer side: a supermarket chain, a township wholesaler, a corner store, a pharmacy. On the supplier side: an importer, a local manufacturer, an agent. Two lists, never mixed. “Supermarket” describes who you sell to and “Importer” who you buy from — they are different questions about the same company, and one that is both is filed on each side separately. Classification only. A category sets no price, no credit limit and no payment terms. Those were agreed with the shop and live on the shop, so that one customer’s terms never depend on a field edited on a different screen. Flat rather than nested: a shop is a supermarket or it is not, and a second level would be filled with guesses.

prices.title: Price levels
prices.help: What each item sells for, at each level. A customer on a level gets that column filled in on their sales lines; a customer on none gets the first. A price belongs to a date. Changing one adds the next price from the day it applies rather than overwriting the last, so an invoice raised in March keeps March’s price — the line records what was actually charged, and this list is only ever the suggestion. A price is per unit, and the unit can be a pack: an item sold in cartons can carry a carton price beside its piece price.

purchasing.title: Purchasing terms
purchasing.help: How long one item takes from one supplier, where it differs from that supplier’s usual lead time. Most items need no row here: leave it blank and the supplier’s own figure is used, and failing that the company default of {days} days. This is the expected lead time — the planned figure replenishment orders against. What the receipts say actually happened is measured separately and shown beside it, and never overwrites what you set here.

Reconciling here instead is for stock that has been found and counted, where no receipt is coming.

int.title: Inventory intelligence
int.help: Which products earn their shelf space, and which have been sitting on it. Worked out from the ledger when this page loads — the revenue is what the invoices say and the cost is what the stock ledger released, so both tie to the profit and loss exactly.
int.pulledBack: pulled back to today — nothing is posted ahead

int.mismatched: {n, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} billed and shipped in different quantities this period.
int.mismatchBody: An invoice recognises the revenue and a delivery releases the cost, and they need not fall in the same window — goods shipped but not yet billed show a cost with no revenue against it, and the margin on that row reads worse than the trade really was. The quantities are shown so the gap is visible.

itemImport.title: Import items
itemImport.help: The item master, from a spreadsheet — what the items are, not how many there are. Quantity and cost are the result of stock documents, so they are not on this sheet; a new item exists with no stock until a goods receipt or an opening stock adjustment gives it some. The spreadsheet is the input and this database stays the source of truth: a row naming a category, brand or unit that does not exist here is refused rather than creating one, because two spellings of the same category is the mess an importer is supposed to prevent. Nothing is written until you confirm, and then all of it is written or none.
itemImport.step1Sub: Excel (.xlsx) or CSV — upload the workbook directly, no need to convert it
itemImport.barcodeText: Format the Barcode column as Text before you fill it.
itemImport.barcodeWhy: Excel treats a long barcode as a number otherwise, which drops any leading zero and rounds anything past fifteen digits — damage done in the sheet, before the file gets here.
itemImport.barcodeTemplate: The Excel template above already has that column formatted, so filling it in is enough.
itemImport.barcodeXlsx: Reading the workbook directly avoids the other half of the problem: a barcode merely displayed as 8.85E+12 is stored exactly, and comes through intact.
itemImport.barcodeCsv: Saving as CSV can also write out the displayed 8.85123E+12 in place of the real number, losing the digits that tell two products apart — uploading the .xlsx avoids that.
itemImport.missingTitle: {n, plural, one {# name is} other {# names are}} not registered yet.
itemImport.missingBody: A category, sub category or brand named in the file has to exist here before an item can point at it — so that items share one spelling of each rather than carrying their own, which is how Coca-Cola, Coca Cola and COKE end up as three brands with a share of the sales each. Add the ones you want; correct the sheet for the rest.
itemImport.looksLike: Looks like “{name}”, which already exists — check the sheet before adding a second.
itemImport.itemMasterNote: what will exist as products — no stock and no cost until a goods receipt or an opening stock adjustment gives them one.
itemImport.codeNote: Code is the identifier the item will carry: its category’s code followed by the Stock ID. A blank Stock ID is given the next number in that category.
itemImport.worthLook: Worth a look, but will not stop the import
itemImport.uploadFirst: Upload a file with no errors to continue.
itemImport.creates: Creates {n, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
itemImport.leaving: , leaving the {n} already here as they are
itemImport.nothingPosted: . Nothing is posted and no stock moves — all of it lands or none of it does.

customerPanel.salesExplain: Total sales counts posted invoices, till sales included. An order counts once it is invoiced, so nothing is counted twice.

customerPanel.activityExplain: From recorded documents and the customer record. Edits to the customer's details are not recorded yet, so they are not shown.
